How is Kansas organized for a home sale?

Kansas is split into 105 counties, and almost every step of a house sale touches a county office. The county appraiser values the property, the county treasurer collects the tax, and the register of deeds records the deed. City hall matters mostly for permits, code violations and utilities.

The counties differ a lot in size. Johnson County is the most populous, and Greeley County is the smallest. That gap shapes how fast a county office answers the phone and how busy its recording desk is.

How do Kansas property taxes work when you sell?

Kansas property tax runs on a fixed yearly calendar set by the Kansas Department of Revenue, and the dates matter for a seller. Counties mail valuation notices for real property by March 1. You have 30 days from the mailing date to file an equalization appeal, and the informal meeting with the county appraiser has to happen by May 15. The appraiser gives a final determination by May 20.

The bill itself comes later in the year. Here are the real property dates from the state calendar.

StepDate
County mails valuation noticesMarch 1
Informal meeting with appraiserMay 15
Appraiser final determinationMay 20
Appraiser certifies values to county clerkJune 1
Tax statements sent by treasurerDecember 1
Full payment or first half dueDecember 20
Second half dueMay 10 of the next year

A spring closing can fall before the second half is paid, so ask the county treasurer for the exact balance before you set a date.

Our guides cover the offices in detail for Sedgwick County, Johnson County and Wyandotte County, plus a statewide Kansas property tax guide. Confirm your own numbers with the county office.

What does recording a deed cost in Kansas?

Recording happens at the register of deeds in the county where the house sits. State law sets the page fees. From 2018 on, the first page of a deed or mortgage is $17 and each added page is $13, based on a Kansas Legislative Research Department memo.

The memo also lists a $1 Heritage Trust Fund fee and a $3 per page technology fee on top of that.

The state also used to charge a mortgage registration tax of 0.26 percent of the secured debt. That tax was phased down from 2015 and repealed in 2019, so a seller today does not see it on a settlement statement for that reason. We did not find a separate state transfer tax in the sources we reviewed, so ask the register of deeds or your title company what applies to your closing.

If you need a simple deed to move title between family members, read our Kansas quitclaim deed guide first, because the wrong deed can slow a sale.

Is foreclosure judicial or non-judicial in Kansas?

Kansas uses judicial foreclosure. The lender files a lawsuit, a judge enters a judgment, and the house is sold at a sheriff's sale. That makes the process slower than in states where a lender can sell without going to court.

A legal summary of the Kansas statutes lays out the main points.

  • A homeowner who is personally served with the suit has 21 days to answer. If notice is by newspaper publication, the answer period is generally 41 days.
  • The lender must publish the notice of sale at least three times, with the last notice running 7 to 14 days before the sale.
  • Deficiency judgments are generally allowed, so a sale for less than the debt can leave a balance.
  • Federal rules usually bar a servicer from starting foreclosure until a loan is more than 120 days past due.

After the sale, Kansas can give the owner time to redeem. The usual period is 12 months from the sale date. If the owner defaulted before one-third of the original debt was repaid, it is three months, and a court can add three months if the owner loses a job after the sale. A court can shorten or end redemption if the property was abandoned.

Selling before the sheriff's sale date keeps control in your hands. The payoff figure has to come from your lender, and an attorney should review any plan once a lawsuit is filed.

How does probate work when you inherit a Kansas house?

Inherited houses in Kansas usually go through the district court in the county where the owner lived. The court appoints a personal representative, and that person signs the deed when the house is sold. Our Kansas probate guide walks through the steps.

Kansas has a shortcut for small estates, but it has limits. Under K.S.A. 59-1507b, when probate assets are $75,000 or less, personal property can go to a successor on an affidavit without letters of administration. That section speaks to personal property, so do not assume it moves title to real estate. Ask the probate court clerk or an attorney how a deed would be handled for your situation.

Some owners avoid probate with a recorded beneficiary deed. We cover that in our transfer on death deed guide, and the estate side of taxes in the estate and inheritance tax guide.

If several heirs share the house, expect every one of them to sign.

How does the Kansas homestead rule affect a sale?

The Kansas homestead protection shields a residence from forced sale by creditors. K.S.A. 60-2301 covers up to 160 acres of farm land, or one acre inside an incorporated city, plus a manufactured or mobile home, when the owner or family lives there.

Two parts of the statute matter to sellers.

  • The protection does not apply to a sale for taxes, or to debts for buying the home or building on it.
  • A homestead cannot be alienated without the joint consent of both spouses when that relationship exists, so both spouses sign the deed.

Our homestead guide covers the tax refund side.

What if tenants live in the house you want to sell?

You can sell a rented house in Kansas, but the landlord rules still apply while a tenant lives there. Under K.S.A. 58-2557, a landlord may enter at reasonable hours after reasonable notice to show the unit to prospective or actual purchasers. Entry without consent is allowed only for an extreme hazard, and the landlord may not use access to harass the tenant.

Ending a tenancy follows set notice rules. For unpaid rent, K.S.A. 58-2564 lets a landlord terminate if the tenant does not pay within three days after written notice, counted as three consecutive 24-hour periods. For other material breaches, the notice must give at least 30 days to terminate if the breach is not fixed within 14 days.

Read our guides on landlord and tenant law and the eviction notice rules before you promise a vacant house to anyone.

What does selling as-is for cash mean in Kansas?

A cash sale as-is means the buyer does not need a mortgage and does not ask you to repair the house first. The buyer checks the property, makes an offer, and closes at a title company or an attorney's office. Closing still involves a deed, a payoff of any liens and a recorded transfer at the register of deeds.

Cash removes the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which often delay a traditional sale. It does not remove the work of clearing title. Unpaid property tax, a lien or a missing heir can stall any buyer.

What property problems come up in Kansas houses?

Radon is the one the Kansas Geological Survey stresses. The EPA action level is 4 picoCuries per liter. The EPA estimates one in 15 homes nationwide is at or above that level, and the Kansas Radon Program says about one in four Kansas homes may be elevated.

The survey adds that radon varies from house to house, so a neighbor's result is no substitute for testing your own. Private wells with dissolved uranium or radium carry the most risk from water. The Kansas Radon Program is based at Kansas State University in Manhattan.

A cash buyer may take radon as part of an as-is deal, but you should still share what you know. For wells or septic, ask the county health office what records exist.

Frequently asked questions

How many counties does Kansas have?

Kansas has 105 counties. Each one has its own appraiser, treasurer and register of deeds, so property tax and recording questions go to the county where the house sits.

Is Kansas foreclosure judicial?

Yes. The lender sues, a judge enters judgment and the house is sold at a sheriff's sale. Redemption after the sale is usually 12 months, but it can be three months in some cases.

When are Kansas property taxes due?

Full payment or the first half is due December 20, and the second half is due May 10 of the next year. Tax statements go out by December 1.

Can I sell an inherited house in Kansas without probate?

Small estates of $75,000 or less can move personal property by affidavit, but that statute addresses personal property. Ask the district court clerk or an attorney how a house deed would be handled.

Do both spouses have to sign when selling a Kansas homestead?

The homestead statute says a homestead cannot be alienated without the joint consent of husband and wife when that relation exists, so plan for both signatures.

Can a landlord show a rented house to buyers?

K.S.A. 58-2557 allows entry at reasonable hours after reasonable notice to show the unit to prospective purchasers. It bars using access to harass the tenant.

Does radon affect Kansas home sales?

It can. The Kansas Radon Program says about one in four Kansas homes may have elevated radon, and only a test of your own house gives a real answer.
